name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+15 district lean with an incumbent Republican running
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~5%
No polls or expert ratings show competitive signals
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Balderson's incumbency and roughly 20-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 5% all point the same way, with no contrary evidence. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: A surge of outside spending or unexpected polling showing Christian within single digits would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
OH-12 is a solidly Republican Columbus-area seat, and incumbent Troy Balderson is seeking another term with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean sits around R+15, and Balderson has built a large financial lead, holding about $2.0 million on hand to challenger Jerrad Christian's roughly $19,000. No independent polls or expert race ratings exist for the contest, so the picture rests on fundamentals.

Prediction markets give Christian only about a 5% chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean and the money gap. The forecast expects Balderson to win by roughly 16 points, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling. Any surprise would likely require substantial outside intervention on the Democratic side late in the cycle.
